newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-MENDEZ TURNS HIS BACK ON ARGENTINA.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-MENDEZ TURNS HIS BACK ON ARGENTINA.

text.p: Argentine hooker Federico Mendez said on Monday he had no plans to play for his country despite being named in a 36-man squad for next month's series against South Africa and December's British tour.

The 24-year-old, who has been playing for South African provincial champions Natal this season, told Reuters he disagreed with his country's amateur policy and that he even entertained hopes of playing for South Africa.
"They (Rugby Union of Argentina) have picked me but I don't think I'm going to play," said Mendez. "I want to play for my province Mendoza against the Springboks in November, but not for my country."

Argentina, who host South Africa for two tests in November before travelling to Britain for internationals against Wales and England, reversed their previous policy of ignoring overseas-based players when they named their 36-man squad on Friday.
Both Mendez (Natal) and experienced lock forward German Llanes (Milan) have been included in the squad.
"The problem is that I don't agree with a few of the laws in Argentina which is the only rugby-playing country in the world which is still 100 percent amateur," Mendez said.

"You can't hope to play and compete against professional players if you're totally amateur. At the moment, it costs you money to play for Argentina -- we aren't paid a single dollar...no match fees, no insurance, not even anything to cover if you've missed a few days at work."
Mendez said he wanted to remain in South Africa, playing with Natal, although he was considering a lucrative offer from English club Bath.
"I really want to stay here in Natal -- the climate is good, it's very good for me and I'm really happy here. But I've had some good offers from overseas and I haven't made my final decision."
On eventually playing for South Africa, Mendez said: "It's a possibility and it could happen in three years."

South African Rugby Football Union (SARFU) media officer Alex Broun said Mendez would become eligible for Springbok selection in February 1999, providing he did not represent Argentina at international level in the future.
